Motivation
The interfaceStateRestoreListenerhas a methodonRestoreSuspendedwhich lets a client observe the restoration of aStateStorewhen thatStateStore's restoration is suspended before it is finished.
StateRestoreListener.onRestoreSuspendedcurrently does not provide the reason for the restoration being suspended. The suspension can happen for one of three reasons:
the task was assigned to another instance
the task was demoted to a standby task on this instance
the instance is shutting down
AStateRestoreListeneris currently unable to differentiate between these reasons even though these reasons may be useful for a Kafka user who, for example, wants to emit observability to diagnose their application.
The analagous listener for standby tasksStateUpdateListenerdoes provide the suspension reason for its analagous method,StateUpdateListener.onUpdateSuspended. Adding the suspension reason to theStateRestoreListener
would fix this mismatch in the listener API.

Changes to StateUpdateListener
StateUpdateListenerwill add a new overload of.onUpdateSuspendthat has the suspension reason as an argument. the old.The new overload will have a default implementation to call the old.onUpdateSuspendwhile dropping the suspension reason.
java
Proposed Changes
SwapKafkaStreams.DelegatingStateRestoreListener.OnRestoreSuspendedto use the new four argument overload
note thatDelegatingStateRestoreListeneris package private, so this is a backwards compatible change
ModifyStateChangelogReader.unregisterto pass the reason it calculates into its call toStateRestoreListener.OnRestoreSuspended(effectively replacing the call to existing.OnRestoreSuspendedwith a call to its overload
Compatibility, Deprecation, and Migration Plan
Kafka 4.X
The existing method will be deprecated but its observable behavior will remain the same to a caller. Existing implementations ofStateRestoreListenerwill remain implementations due to the use of a default method.
This ensures that backwards compatibility will remain during 4.X releases.
Kafka 5.0
When Kafka 5.0 releases, we can remove the deprecated original overload ofStateRestoreListener.OnRestoreSuspended. This is a backwards breaking change.
Test Plan
Unit tests for new method overload
Enforce that an implementation that does not explicitly define the new overload ofOnRestoresSuspendedis still able to implementStateRestoreListener (likely through an anonymous implementation in a unit test)
Rejected Alternatives
Defining a new interface that extends from StateRestoreListener that adds this overload
this was rejected because using a default method for the new overload provided a cleaner way of adding the change without breaking backwards compatability
